topics.topic: Whether post-commit authorization checks on in-flight requests must observe revocation
questions: If a request authenticates before revocation commits but performs its project authorization check afterward, must that check observe the revocation?

If a request authenticates before revocation commits but performs its project-scope or capability check after the commit, must that request be rejected or may it continue using the pre-revocation authentication result?
If a request passes authentication before revocation commits but performs its project-scope or capability check afterward, must that request observe the revocation?

quotes:
A4: `rules.project_guard_sequence` in order — `valid_session`,
`active_principal`, `project_access`, `required_capability`,
`registry_lifecycle` — first failure winning; session, account and
assignment are read from persistence in one transaction; an administrator
passes the single-area scope, an operator needs an active assignment (A1,
A2, A5).

A4 as for staff reads; project access is an active `ProjectViewerGrant` read
from persistence; archived projects are readable (A5).
judgement.why: State 5 decides that the project guard rereads the session, account, assignment or viewer grant from persistence, so a revocation committed before that guard transaction is observed even if initial request authentication occurred earlier.

topics.topic: Module ownership of archived progress-read manual-budget creation
questions: Which module owns the decision and mechanism that a staff progress-list read creates an empty manual budget for an archived project?

quotes: `module:budget_management`. Return the project's one manual budget version, creating it empty when absent.
`module:project_tracking`. List the project's recorded section progress in plan order.

Not a pure read: when the project has no manual budget version, this list
creates it empty with its `budget.manual_version_create` audit, exactly as
`ensure_manual_budget` does, an archived project included; otherwise
read-only.
judgement.why: State 5 assigns the progress-list operation to project_tracking and the manual-budget creation mechanism to budget_management.ensure_manual_budget, with project_tracking explicitly named as its caller.

topics.topic: Source and timing of the bootstrap audit record timestamp
questions: Who supplies `occurred_at` for the bootstrap audit record, and is it the bootstrap operation's single timestamp or a separate append-time clock reading?

quotes:
The one exception is the audit record's `occurred_at`: the audit
writer takes it when it appends (Factory code `application/audit_writer.py`
136).

The one record not written
through it is the bootstrap's `staff.create`: `staff_bootstrap` builds that
record itself and `staff_bootstrap_store` inserts it (A29; Factory code
`application/staff_bootstrap.py`).

A29: the first-administrator operation — normalize and validate the input
through `staff_identity`'s input boundary, hash the password through
`credential_security`, build the administrator account and its audit, and ask
`StaffBootstrapPort` to create it only on an empty staff table; refuse with
`BootstrapAlreadyCompleted` otherwise. Factory `6011ac93b143` (R0-07).

The persistence of the first-administrator bootstrap (A29): its own
connection, an exclusive write transaction, the emptiness check of the staff
table and the two inserts (account and its `staff.create` audit), committed
once or not at all. Factory `6011ac93b143`.
judgement.divergence: One implementation gives the bootstrap audit the operation timestamp used for the account; another takes a separate clock reading when the bootstrap audit is inserted, and an auditor comparing the account and audit timestamps notices the difference.
judgement.why: The bootstrap bypasses audit_writer, but the texts assign audit occurred_at only to audit_writer and do not assign its clock reading to staff_bootstrap or staff_bootstrap_store.

witness.initial: The deployment has no staff account, and time advances between construction of the first administrator and insertion of its audit record.
events: The host operator runs the local bootstrap command.
staff_bootstrap constructs the administrator and its staff.create audit.
staff_bootstrap_store inserts both records in its exclusive transaction.
outcomes: The audit occurred_at equals the administrator's created_at because staff_bootstrap supplies the operation's timestamp.
The audit occurred_at is later because the bootstrap path takes a separate append-time clock reading.
witness.observer: An administrator or auditor comparing the persisted administrator and staff.create audit timestamps.
basis:
The host operator runs a local administrative command that creates exactly one active, verified
administrator when no staff account exists, and is refused once any exists.

The one record not written
through it is the bootstrap's `staff.create`: `staff_bootstrap` builds that
record itself and `staff_bootstrap_store` inserts it (A29; Factory code
`application/staff_bootstrap.py`).

The persistence of the first-administrator bootstrap (A29): its own
connection, an exclusive write transaction, the emptiness check of the staff
table and the two inserts (account and its `staff.create` audit), committed
once or not at all. Factory `6011ac93b143`.

topics.topic: Transaction boundary between empty manual-budget creation and progress read
questions: Must creation of the empty manual budget and the progress read occur in one transaction, or may `project_tracking` call `budget_management.ensure_manual_budget` as a separately committed operation before performing its read?

quotes:
The tracking read transaction closes before
`budget_management.ensure_manual_budget` is called for the order.

Not a pure read: when the project has no manual budget version, this list
creates it empty with its `budget.manual_version_create` audit, exactly as
`ensure_manual_budget` does, an archived project included; otherwise
read-only.
judgement.why: State 5 explicitly decides that the tracking read transaction closes before the separately transactional manual-budget creation call.
